newsitem.title: UK: Northern set to appeal takeover deadline.
newsitem.headline: Northern set to appeal takeover deadline.

text.p: Britain's Takeover Panel said on Monday that Northern Electric Plc and its brokers, BZW, indicated they wished to appeal the watchdog's decision to extend the deadline on a hostile bid for the UK utility.

The panel decided late on Friday to extend the deadline for CE Electric's bid until 1300 GMT on Christmas Eve, apparently because BZW did not initially disclose an extra 250,000 pound fee related to its performance in the bid.
Northern Electric set to appeal deadline
At Northern's request, dealing in its shares was temporarily suspended from 0730 GMT on Monday, pending the conclusion of the appeal process.
The panel said it would meet later on Monday morning to hear Northern and BZW's applications for leave to appeal. If granted, an appeal committee will meet as soon as possible thereafter.

CE's 782 million pound ($1.30 billion) offer for Northern had been scheduled to close at 1300 GMT on Friday, with the U.S.-controlled company falling fractionally short of the number of shareholder acceptances needed to win.
But CE, controlled by CalEnergy Co Inc, said on Saturday it had received late acceptances that tipped it over the 50 percent mark needed for victory.

Acceptances for the bid received by CE after the original deadline must be approved by the panel. The panel said it would not publish its reason for extending the bid until the outcome of the appeal process was known.
Over the weekend, industry sources said newspaper reports attributing the extension to the fee structure had drawn a reasonable conclusion.
A win by CE would leave only two of Britain's 12 regional electricity companies (Recs) independent -- Yorkshire Electricity and Southern Electric. ($1=.6002 Pound)
